construct: Collider bias occurs when analysis conditions on, stratifies by, or selects participants according to a variable that is a common effect of both an exposure and an outcome (or their causes). Conditioning on the collider can induce a spurious association between otherwise independent variables.

adversarial_second_pass.independent_reconstruction: Hospital admission is caused by both exposure and disease; restricting analysis to hospitalized patients conditions on their common effect and can induce a spurious exposure-disease association—collider/Berkson bias.
adversarial_second_pass.strongest_distractor_attack: Recall, lead-time, verification, and attrition biases each require mechanisms absent from the stem. The explicit conditioning on hospital admission, itself caused by both variables, is the defining collider/Berkson structure.
